source.text: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν;

records.literal_gloss: What then will we say?

en.L: What then will we say?
en.B: What then are we to say?
en.R: So what should we say about this?

es.L: ¿Qué, pues, diremos?
es.B: ¿Qué diremos entonces?
es.R: Entonces, ¿qué debemos decir de esto?

sw.L: Basi tutasema nini?
sw.B: Basi, tuseme nini?
sw.R: Basi, tunapaswa kusema nini kuhusu jambo hili?

fr.L: Que dirons-nous donc ?
fr.B: Que dire alors ?
fr.R: Alors, que faut-il dire de cela ?

ko.L: 그러면 우리가 무엇이라고 말하겠습니까?
ko.B: 그렇다면 우리는 무엇이라고 말해야 하겠습니까?
ko.R: 그러면 우리는 이 일에 대해 무엇이라고 말해야 하겠습니까?

decisions.choice: a question that opens the next step of the argument
decisions.reason: Paul asks what follows from what he has just said: that where sin increased, grace increased all the more (5:20). He uses the same question in 4:1, 8:31 and 9:14.

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level, as in chapter 5
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Romans is a letter: Paul tells his readers what God has done for them, which French says with the passé composé.

decisions.choice: 합쇼체 with "여러분" and "우리" continues; {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}; no deity_pronoun spans (as through the letter)
decisions.reason: As settled at 1:1: the letter is in 합쇼체 at every level, Paul's rhetorical questions included, and Korean has no deity_pronoun spans because there are no capital letters for the setting to change; respect for God and Christ is carried by -시- and 께서.

source.text: ἐπιμένωμεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ἵνα ἡ χάρις πλεονάσῃ;

records.literal_gloss: Shall we continue in the sin, that the grace may abound?

en.L: Should we remain in sin, so that grace may increase?
en.B: Are we to stay on in sin, so that grace may increase all the more?
en.R: Should we keep living in sin, so that God can show even more of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace?

es.L: ¿Hemos de permanecer en el pecado, para que la gracia aumente?
es.B: ¿Vamos a quedarnos en el pecado, para que la gracia crezca todavía más?
es.R: ¿Debemos seguir viviendo en pecado, para que Dios muestre todavía más {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia?

sw.L: Je, tuendelee kukaa katika dhambi, ili neema iongezeke?
sw.B: Je, tubaki ndani ya dhambi, ili neema iongezeke zaidi?
sw.R: Je, tuendelee kuishi katika dhambi, ili Mungu aonyeshe neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} zaidi na zaidi?

fr.L: Demeurerons-nous dans le péché, afin que la grâce abonde ?
fr.B: Faut-il rester dans le péché pour que la grâce soit encore plus abondante ?
fr.R: Allons-nous continuer à vivre dans le péché, pour que Dieu montre encore plus {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce ?

ko.L: 은혜가 많아지게 하려고 우리가 죄 안에 머물러 있어야 하겠습니까?
ko.B: 은혜가 더욱 넘치게 하려고 우리가 계속 죄 가운데 머물러 있어야 하겠습니까?
ko.R: 하나님께서 은혜를 더 많이 베푸시게 하려고 우리가 계속 죄를 지으며 살아야 하겠습니까?

decisions.reason: Paul had said that where sin increased, grace increased even more (5:20). Someone could twist that into a reason to go on sinning. Some were already accusing Paul of teaching "let us do evil so that good may come" (3:8).

decisions.choice: remain in: go on living in sin as in a place one stays
alternatives: continue in the practice of sinning
decisions.reason: epimenō is to stay on or persist. With "in sin" it pictures sin as the place or power a person lives under, which verse 2 takes up: "how will we still live in it?"

decisions.choice: sin: the power, not single acts
decisions.reason: The Greek has "the sin", with the article, as all through 5:12-21 and this chapter. Sin is pictured as a power that reigns, enslaves and pays wages (5:21, 6:6, 6:23).

decisions.choice: so that God can show even more of his grace
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver of grace, which the Greek leaves understood.

decisions.choice: "죄 안에 머물러 있다" (L); "죄 가운데 머물러 있다" (B); "계속 죄를 지으며 살다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as staying on in sin as in a place one lives. "머물러 있다" keeps that picture at Literal and Balanced; Readable says plainly what it means.

source.text: μὴ γένοιτο· οἵτινες ἀπεθάνομεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, πῶς ἔτι ζήσομεν ἐν αὐτῇ;

records.literal_gloss: Not may it be; who died to the sin, how still shall we live in it?

en.L: May it not be! We who died to sin, how will we still live in it?
en.B: Certainly not! We are people who died to sin; how could we still be living in it?
en.R: Of course not! We have died to sin. So how could we keep on living in it?

es.L: ¡No sea así! Nosotros, que morimos al pecado, ¿cómo todavía viviremos en él?
es.B: ¡De ningún modo! Somos de los que murieron al pecado: ¿cómo podríamos seguir viviendo en él?
es.R: ¡Claro que no! Hemos muerto al pecado. Entonces, ¿cómo podríamos seguir viviendo en él?

sw.L: Isiwe hivyo! Sisi tulioifia dhambi, tutaishije bado ndani yake?
sw.B: Hasha! Sisi ni watu walioifia dhambi; tungewezaje kuendelea kuishi ndani yake?
sw.R: Sivyo kabisa! Tumekwisha kuifia dhambi. Basi tungewezaje kuendelea kuishi ndani yake?

fr.L: Qu’il n’en soit rien ! Nous qui sommes morts au péché, comment vivrons-nous encore en lui ?
fr.B: Absolument pas ! Nous sommes des gens qui sont morts au péché ; comment pourrions-nous encore y vivre ?
fr.R: Pas du tout ! Nous sommes morts au péché. Alors comment pourrions-nous continuer à y vivre ?

ko.L: 결코 그럴 수 없습니다! 죄에 대하여 죽은 우리가 어떻게 아직도 그 안에서 살겠습니까?
ko.B: 절대로 그렇지 않습니다! 우리는 죄에 대해 죽은 사람들입니다. 그런데 어떻게 아직도 죄 가운데 살 수 있겠습니까?
ko.R: 절대 아닙니다! 우리는 죄에 대해서는 이미 죽었습니다. 그런데 어떻게 계속 죄 가운데 살 수 있겠습니까?

decisions.reason: mē genoito, "may it not happen", is Paul's strongest way of rejecting a false conclusion (3:4, 3:6, 6:15, 9:14, 11:1).
Balanced and Readable use ordinary English for an emphatic no, as 3:4 and 9:14 do. "God forbid" adds a word for God that the Greek does not have.

decisions.choice: died to sin: our life under sin's rule has ended
decisions.reason: To die to something is to be finished with it, beyond its reach. The death meant is the believer's share in Christ's death (verses 3-6). It does not say believers no longer feel the pull of sin; verses 12-13 still urge them not to let it reign.

decisions.choice: who: people of such a kind
decisions.reason: hoitines often means "people who are such that". The point is what kind of people believers are: people who have died to sin.

decisions.choice: ¡No sea así! (L); ¡De ningún modo! (B); ¡Claro que no! (R)
decisions.reason: As in 3:4, 3:6, 9:14 and 11:1, the same Spanish is used at each level wherever Romans has Paul's strongest no: here and in 6:15.
As in 3:4, 3:6, 9:14 and 11:1, the same Swahili is used at each level wherever Romans has Paul's strongest no: here and in 6:15.

"Died to sin" is said with the applied form of the verb, "kuifia dhambi" (to die with respect to sin): the death ends sin's claim (m2). "Kufa kwa dhambi" would mean dying of sin or because of sin. The chapter keeps the same form in 6:10 and 6:11 ("aliifia dhambi", "mmeifia dhambi"), and Literal says "living to God" the same way ("kumwishia Mungu").

decisions.choice: "Qu’il n’en soit rien !" (L); "Absolument pas !" (B); "Pas du tout !" (R) (for the whole letter, as in 3:4)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the wish form of the Greek, "may it not be". "À Dieu ne plaise" adds a word for God the Greek does not have, as the English decision says of "God forbid". Balanced and Readable use ordinary French for an emphatic no.

decisions.choice: "결코 그럴 수 없습니다!" (L); "절대로 그렇지 않습니다!" (B); "절대 아닙니다!" (R)
decisions.reason: As settled at 3:4 for the whole letter: the three levels keep one fixed Korean form each for this strongest denial, so the reader hears the same cry each time Paul uses it.

decisions.choice: "죄에 대하여 죽다" (L); "죄에 대해 죽다" (B, R), through the chapter
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says that the life under sin's rule has ended. "죄에 대하여 죽다" keeps Paul's picture of death at every level, so that it can be set beside Christ's death to sin in verse 10 and "living to God" in verse 11.

source.text: ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε ὅτι ὅσοι ἐβαπτίσθημεν εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθημεν;

records.literal_gloss: Or are you unaware that as many as were baptized into Christ Jesus into the death of him were baptized?

en.L: Or are you unaware that as many [of us] as were baptized into {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus were baptized into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death?
en.B: Or have you not grasped that everyone among us who was baptized into {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus was baptized into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death?
en.R: Surely you know that when we were baptized and joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, we were also joined to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death.

es.L: ¿O {{plural_you:ignoran|ignoráis}} que todos los que fuimos bautizados en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}} fuimos bautizados en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} muerte?
es.B: ¿O no {{plural_you:han comprendido|habéis comprendido}} que todos los que fuimos bautizados en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}} fuimos bautizados en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} muerte?
es.R: Seguro que {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que, cuando fuimos bautizados y unidos {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}, también fuimos unidos a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} muerte.

sw.L: Au hamjui kwamba sisi sote tuliobatizwa kuingia katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu tulibatizwa kuingia katika kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}?
sw.B: Au hamjatambua kwamba kila mmoja wetu aliyebatizwa kuingia katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu alibatizwa kuingia katika kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}?
sw.R: Hakika mnajua kwamba tulipobatizwa tuliunganishwa na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, na hivyo tuliunganishwa pia na kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}.

fr.L: Ou ignorez-vous que nous tous qui avons été baptisés {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, c’est en {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mort que nous avons été baptisés ?
fr.B: Ou n’avez-vous pas compris que nous tous qui avons été baptisés {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, nous avons été baptisés en {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mort ?
fr.R: Vous le savez bien : quand nous avons été baptisés et unis au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, nous avons aussi été unis à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mort.

ko.L: 혹은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 안으로 세례를 받은 우리 모두가 그분의 죽음 안으로 세례를 받았다는 것을 여러분은 알지 못합니까?
ko.B: 아니면 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수와 하나가 되는 세례를 받은 우리가 모두 그분의 죽음과 하나가 되는 세례를 받았다는 것을 여러분은 모릅니까?
ko.R: 여러분은 분명히 알고 있을 것입니다. 우리가 세례를 받고 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수와 하나가 되었을 때, 우리는 그분의 죽음과도 하나가 되었습니다.

decisions.choice: baptized into Christ Jesus: brought into union with him
decisions.reason: To be baptized "into" someone is to be joined to him and to belong to him (Galatians 3:27; 1 Corinthians 10:2, "baptized into Moses"). Joined to Christ, the believer is joined to what happened to him, his death first of all.

decisions.choice: or: a reminder of what they should already know
decisions.reason: Paul asks whether they have missed what their baptism meant. The question assumes they know it, as in 7:1.
Readable says what "baptized into" means: joined to Christ and to his death. It keeps "baptized" once, so the act itself is still named.
Readable turns the question into a statement, since Paul expects the answer yes.

"Into" here means being brought into union with him (m1). "Katika" alone would read as a place or a setting ("baptized in Christ"), so Literal and Balanced say "kuingia katika" (into). Readable says "tuliunganishwa na" (we were joined to), as the English Readable does.

"Kifo" is the ordinary standard word for death, used in 1:32; "mauti" is older and more literary. The chapter uses "kifo" throughout, including for death as a power that rules (6:9) and pays wages (6:23).

"Baptized into Christ" uses the same span as Paul's "in Christ": the familiar "en Christ" by default, "dans le Messie" as the alternative, so that the French keeps the sense of being brought into union with him.

decisions.choice: "... 안으로 세례를 받다" (L); "... 와 하나가 되는 세례를 받다" (B); "세례를 받고 ... 와 하나가 되다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads baptism "into" Christ as being brought into union with him. Literal keeps the preposition as "안으로"; Balanced and Readable say the union with "하나가 되다", and do the same for "into his death" so the two phrases stay parallel.

source.text: συνετάφημεν οὖν αὐτῷ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος εἰς τὸν θάνατον, ἵνα ὥσπερ ἠγέρθη Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ πατρός, οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς περιπατήσωμεν.

records.literal_gloss: We were buried with therefore him through the baptism into the death, that just as was raised Christ out of dead [ones] through the glory of the Father, so also we in newness of life should walk.

en.L: Therefore we were buried with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} through baptism into death, so that just as {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} was raised from [the] dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.
en.B: So through baptism we were buried with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} into death, in order that, as {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might live a life that is new.
en.R: When we were baptized, it was as if we were buried with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and shared {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death. {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} was raised from the dead by the glorious power of the Father. In the same way, we too are to live a completely new life.

es.L: Por tanto, fuimos sepultados con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por medio del bautismo en la muerte, para que, así como {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} fue resucitado de entre [los] muertos por medio de la gloria del Padre, así también nosotros caminemos en novedad de vida.
es.B: Así que, por medio del bautismo, fuimos sepultados con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en la muerte, a fin de que, como {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} fue resucitado de entre los muertos por la gloria del Padre, también nosotros vivamos una vida nueva.
es.R: Cuando fuimos bautizados, fue como si nos sepultaran con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y compartiéramos {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} muerte. {{christos:Cristo|El Mesías}} fue resucitado de entre los muertos por el glorioso poder del Padre. Del mismo modo, también nosotros debemos vivir una vida completamente nueva.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo tulizikwa pamoja na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kupitia ubatizo kuingia katika kifo, ili, sawa na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alivyofufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu kupitia utukufu wa Baba, nasi pia tutembee katika hali mpya ya uzima.
sw.B: Basi kupitia ubatizo tulizikwa pamoja na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} katika kifo, ili kama {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alivyofufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu kwa utukufu wa Baba, sisi pia tuishi maisha mapya.
sw.R: Tulipobatizwa, ilikuwa kana kwamba tulizikwa pamoja na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} na kushiriki kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}. {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alifufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu kwa nguvu tukufu za Baba. Vivyo hivyo, sisi pia tunapaswa kuishi maisha mapya kabisa.

fr.L: Nous avons donc été ensevelis avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} par le baptême dans la mort, afin que, comme {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} a été ressuscité d’entre [les] morts par la gloire du Père, de même nous aussi nous marchions dans une vie nouvelle.
fr.B: Par le baptême, nous avons donc été ensevelis avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dans la mort, afin que, comme {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} a été ressuscité d’entre les morts par la gloire du Père, nous aussi, nous vivions une vie nouvelle.
fr.R: Quand nous avons été baptisés, c’est comme si nous avions été enterrés avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et que nous avions partagé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mort. Le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} a été ressuscité d’entre les morts par la puissance glorieuse du Père. De la même façon, nous aussi, nous devons vivre une vie toute nouvelle.

ko.L: 그러므로 우리는 죽음 안으로 [들어가는] 세례를 통하여 그분과 함께 묻혔습니다. 이는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 아버지의 영광을 통하여 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나신 것과 같이, 우리도 새로운 생명 가운데서 걸어가게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 우리는 그분의 죽음과 하나가 되는 세례를 통해 그분과 함께 묻혔습니다. 이는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 아버지의 영광으로 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나신 것처럼, 우리도 새로운 생명으로 살아가게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.R: 우리가 세례를 받았을 때, 우리는 마치 그분과 함께 묻혀서 그분의 죽음을 함께 겪은 것과 같습니다. {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 아버지의 영광스러운 능력으로 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나셨습니다. 그와 같이 우리도 완전히 새로운 삶을 살아야 합니다.

decisions.choice: into death goes with baptism: the baptism that joins us to his death
alternatives: buried ... into death (death as the place of burial)
decisions.reason: The words "into death" pick up verse 3, "baptized into his death". The burial is the sign that the death was real; it is through baptism that believers share it.

decisions.choice: the glory of the Father: his glorious power
decisions.reason: God's glory is the shining out of who he is. Here it is his power at work in raising Jesus, as "glory" and "power" stand side by side in Colossians 1:11 and 2 Thessalonians 1:9.
To "walk" is a Hebrew way of speaking of how a person lives day by day. "Newness of life" is a life of a new kind, the life of the age to come begun now.
Balanced and Readable say what "walk" means. Literal keeps the picture.
Readable makes clear that the burial is shared through baptism, not literally.
Readable joins "glory" to the power it means here (see the meaning decision on the glory of the Father).

The style guide keeps "uzima" for life (zōē), and Literal does ("hali mpya ya uzima"). But "walk in newness of life" is about how one lives day by day (m3), which is what "maisha" names, so Balanced and Readable say "tuishi maisha mapya".
"En nouveauté de vie" copies the Greek but is not French; "une vie nouvelle" keeps the noun "life" and the newness, while "marcher" keeps the picture of walking.

decisions.choice: "새로운 생명 가운데서 걸어가다" (L); "새로운 생명으로 살아가다" (B); "새로운 삶을 살다" (R)
decisions.reason: Walking is the Greek picture for how one lives (meaning decision). Literal keeps "걸어가다"; Balanced and Readable say "살아가다", "살다". "생명" is kept at Literal and Balanced to tie the phrase to "eternal life" (verses 22-23).

source.text: Εἰ γὰρ σύμφυτοι γεγόναμεν τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἐσόμεθα·

records.literal_gloss: If for united we have become in the likeness of the death of him, but also of the resurrection we will be;

en.L: For if we have become united with the likeness of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death, we will certainly also be [united with the likeness] of [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] resurrection;
en.B: For if we have grown into one with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the likeness of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death, we will certainly be one with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the likeness of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} resurrection as well.
en.R: We have become one with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by going through something like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death. So we will surely become one with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by going through something like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rising to life too.

es.L: Porque si hemos llegado a estar unidos con la semejanza de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} muerte, ciertamente también lo estaremos [con la semejanza] de [{{deity_pronoun:su|Su}}] resurrección;
es.B: Porque si hemos crecido hasta ser uno con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en la semejanza de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} muerte, sin duda también seremos uno con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en la semejanza de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} resurrección.
es.R: Nos hemos hecho uno con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} al pasar por algo semejante a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} muerte. Por eso, sin duda también seremos uno con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} al pasar por algo semejante a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vuelta a la vida.

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa tumefanywa kuwa kitu kimoja na mfano wa kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}, hakika tutakuwa pia [kitu kimoja na mfano] wa ufufuo [{{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}];
sw.B: Kwa maana ikiwa tumekua na kuwa kitu kimoja na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} katika mfano wa kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}, hakika tutakuwa kitu kimoja na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} pia katika mfano wa ufufuo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Tumekuwa kitu kimoja na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kwa kupitia jambo linalofanana na kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}. Kwa hiyo hakika tutakuwa kitu kimoja na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kwa kupitia jambo linalofanana na kufufuka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} pia.

fr.L: Car si nous avons été unis à la ressemblance de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mort, nous le serons certainement aussi [à la ressemblance] de [{{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}}] résurrection ;
fr.B: Car si nous avons été greffés sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} en partageant une mort semblable à la {{deity_pronoun:sienne|Sienne}}, nous partagerons certainement aussi une résurrection semblable à la {{deity_pronoun:sienne|Sienne}}.
fr.R: Nous avons été unis à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} en passant par quelque chose de semblable à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mort. Alors, c’est sûr, nous serons aussi unis à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} en passant par quelque chose de semblable à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} retour à la vie.

ko.L: 만일 우리가 그분의 죽음과 같은 모양으로 [그분과] 연합한 사람이 되었다면, 반드시 그분의 부활과 같은 모양으로도 [연합한 사람이] 될 것입니다.
ko.B: 우리가 그분의 죽음과 같은 모습으로 그분과 하나로 자라났다면, 그분의 부활과 같은 모습으로도 분명히 그분과 하나가 될 것입니다.
ko.R: 우리는 그분이 죽으신 것과 같은 일을 겪어서 그분과 하나가 되었습니다. 그러므로 우리는 그분이 다시 살아나신 것과 같은 일도 겪어서 틀림없이 그분과 하나가 될 것입니다.

decisions.reason: symphytos is used of things that grow together, like a graft that becomes one with the plant. It describes a close and living union.

decisions.choice: united with him by the likeness of his death
decisions.reason: The Greek can mean "united with the likeness of his death" or "united with him in the likeness of his death". Verses 4 and 8 speak of dying and living with Christ, so the union is with him, and the likeness is the way believers share his death, through baptism (verse 4). Literal keeps the Greek's shorter form.

decisions.choice: we will be: a sure future, already at work now
decisions.reason: The future may point to the resurrection of the body at the end (8:11) or to the new life that follows from the believer's union with Christ now (verse 4). Verse 8 also uses the future. Both are likely in view; the words are left as a future.

decisions.choice: [united with the likeness] (L); be one with him in the likeness (B)
decisions.reason: The second half of the Greek leaves the words of the first half to be understood. Literal supplies them in brackets, Balanced in full.
Balanced keeps the growing picture in symphytos.

decisions.choice: going through something like his death / his rising to life
decisions.reason: Readable explains "likeness" and says "rising to life" for resurrection.

The word means grown together into one (m1). "Kuwa kitu kimoja na" (to become one thing with) says the union more fully than "kuunganishwa na" (to be joined to), and Balanced adds "tumekua" (we have grown), as the English Balanced keeps the picture of growth.

The Greek word pictures things that grow together, like a graft that becomes one with the plant (see the meaning decision). French "greffés" keeps that picture in one ordinary word, as the English Balanced keeps it with "grown into one".

The word means grown together, like two plants (meaning decision). Literal uses the plain "연합하다"; Balanced keeps the picture of growing; Readable says the result simply. "접붙임" belongs to a different picture (11:17-24) and is avoided here.

source.text: τοῦτο γινώσκοντες ὅτι ὁ παλαιὸς ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος συνεσταυρώθη, ἵνα καταργηθῇ τὸ σῶμα τῆς ἁμαρτίας, τοῦ μηκέτι δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ὁ γὰρ ἀποθανὼν δεδικαίωται ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας.

records.literal_gloss: this knowing that the old of us self was crucified with, that might be done away with the body of the sin, [for] the no longer to be enslaved us to the sin; \v 7 the [one] for having died has been justified from the sin.

en.L: knowing this, that our old self was crucified with [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], so that the body of sin might be made powerless, so that we would no longer be enslaved to sin; \v 7 for the one who has died has been justified from sin.
en.B: We know this: our old self was nailed to the cross with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that the body of sin would be stripped of its power and we would no longer serve sin as slaves. \v 7 For anyone who has died is declared free from sin.
en.R: We know that the people we used to be were put to death on the cross with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. This happened so that the self that sin ruled would be put out of action, and we would no longer be slaves to sin. \v 7 Anyone who has died is free from sin's claim.

es.L: sabiendo esto, que nuestro viejo yo fue crucificado con [{{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}], para que el cuerpo del pecado quedara sin poder, a fin de que ya no estemos esclavizados al pecado; \v 7 porque el que murió ha quedado justificado del pecado.
es.B: Sabemos esto: nuestro viejo yo fue clavado en la cruz con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, para que el cuerpo del pecado fuera despojado de su poder y ya no sirviéramos al pecado como esclavos. \v 7 Porque quien ha muerto queda declarado libre del pecado.
es.R: Sabemos que las personas que éramos antes fueron llevadas a la muerte en la cruz junto con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}. Esto sucedió para que el yo que el pecado gobernaba quedara fuera de combate, y ya no fuéramos esclavos del pecado. \v 7 El que ha muerto queda libre del derecho que el pecado tenía sobre él.

sw.L: tukijua hili, kwamba nafsi yetu ya zamani ilisulubiwa pamoja [na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}], ili mwili wa dhambi uondolewe nguvu, ili tusiwe tena chini ya utumwa wa dhambi; \v 7 kwa maana aliyekufa amehesabiwa haki mbali na dhambi.
sw.B: Tunajua hili: nafsi yetu ya zamani ilipigiliwa msalabani pamoja na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, ili mwili wa dhambi unyang'anywe nguvu zake, nasi tusiwe tena watumwa wanaoitumikia dhambi. \v 7 Kwa maana yeyote aliyekufa ametangazwa kuwa huru mbali na dhambi.
sw.R: Tunajua kwamba yule mtu tuliyekuwa zamani aliuawa msalabani pamoja na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Hili lilitokea ili nafsi iliyotawaliwa na dhambi iondolewe nguvu, nasi tusiwe tena watumwa wa dhambi. \v 7 Mtu aliyekufa yuko huru: dhambi haina tena dai lolote juu yake.

fr.L: sachant ceci, que {{gender:notre être ancien|notre vieil homme}} a été crucifié avec [{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], afin que le corps du péché soit réduit à l’impuissance, pour que nous ne soyons plus esclaves du péché ; \v 7 car celui qui est mort a été justifié du péché.
fr.B: Nous le savons : {{gender:l’être que nous étions autrefois|notre vieil homme}} a été cloué à la croix avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, afin que le corps du péché soit privé de sa force et que nous ne soyons plus esclaves du péché. \v 7 Car celui qui est mort est justifié et libéré du péché.
fr.R: Nous savons que ce que nous étions avant a été mis à mort sur la croix avec le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. C’est arrivé pour que notre être dominé par le péché soit mis hors d’état d’agir, et que nous ne soyons plus esclaves du péché. \v 7 Celui qui est mort, le péché n’a plus aucun droit sur lui.

ko.L: 우리는 이것을 압니다. 우리의 옛 사람이 [그분과] 함께 십자가에 못 박힌 것은 죄의 몸이 무력하게 되어, 우리가 더 이상 죄에게 종노릇 하지 않게 하려는 것입니다. \v 7 죽은 사람은 죄에서 벗어나 의롭다고 인정받았기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 우리가 알듯이, 우리의 옛 사람은 그분과 함께 십자가에 못 박혔습니다. 그것은 죄의 몸이 힘을 잃고, 우리가 더 이상 죄의 종으로 섬기지 않게 하려는 것입니다. \v 7 죽은 사람은 죄에서 풀려났다고 선언을 받았기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 우리는 알고 있습니다. 예전의 우리는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}와 함께 십자가에 못 박혀 죽었습니다. 그래서 죄가 다스리던 우리 자신은 힘을 잃었고, 우리는 더 이상 죄의 종이 아닙니다. \v 7 죽은 사람에게는 죄가 더 이상 아무런 권리도 주장할 수 없습니다.

decisions.choice: our old self: the person we were under sin's rule
decisions.reason: The "old self" is not a part of a person but the whole person as he or she was in Adam, before being joined to Christ (5:12-21; Ephesians 4:22; Colossians 3:9).

decisions.choice: the body of sin: the self under the rule of sin
decisions.reason: The body is the person as one who lives and acts in the world. "Of sin" says who has been ruling it. The body itself is not evil; verse 13 urges believers to give its parts to God.

decisions.choice: made powerless: put out of action
decisions.reason: katargeō means to make ineffective, to take out of use. The old order of sin loses its hold, though verses 12-13 show the struggle is real.

decisions.choice: justified from sin: declared free from sin's claim
alternatives: set free from sin (without the legal sense)
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in Romans dikaioō means God declares people righteous (3:24, 5:1). Here, with "from sin", it has a legal sense: as death ends a person's debts and legal claims, the one who has died with Christ is acquitted and released from sin's claim. It may also echo a saying that death settles all accounts.

decisions.choice: declared free (B); free from sin's claim (R)
decisions.reason: Here dikaioō means acquittal and release, not being counted righteous, so Balanced says "declared free" and Readable "free from sin's claim" instead of the usual "declared righteous".

decisions.choice: the people we used to be
decisions.reason: Readable explains "old self" in plain words.

decisions.choice: put to death on the cross with Christ
decisions.reason: Readable names Christ, whom the Greek leaves understood, and explains "crucified with".

decisions.choice: nuestro viejo yo (L, B); las personas que éramos antes (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the phrase as the person we were under sin's rule (m1). "Viejo hombre" is the traditional church phrase, but to a new reader it says "old man"; "viejo yo" names the self, as "old self" does. Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: ha quedado justificado (L); queda declarado libre (B); queda libre del derecho que el pecado tenía sobre él (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "justificar", the settled verb. Here it means a verdict that also releases: the one who has died is acquitted and set free from sin's claim (m4). Balanced and Readable say that, as the English does.

The phrase means the person we were under sin's rule (m1). "Nafsi" (the self, the person) says that directly; "utu wa kale" is the established phrase of older versions and may be what readers expect. A reviewer should choose.

decisions.choice: amehesabiwa haki mbali na dhambi (L); ametangazwa kuwa huru mbali na dhambi (B); yuko huru: dhambi haina tena dai lolote juu yake (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "kuhesabiwa haki", the settled verb, with "mbali na" (away from) for the Greek "from". The sense is a verdict that also releases: the one who has died is acquitted and freed from sin's claim (m4). Balanced says "declared free" and Readable "sin no longer has any claim on him", as the English does.
"Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery itself is the point: slavery to sin, set against being freed from it (6:7).

decisions.choice: {{gender:notre être ancien|notre vieil homme}} (L); {{gender:l'être que nous étions autrefois|notre vieil homme}} (B)
decisions.reason: The English "old self" needs no setting, but the traditional French "le vieil homme" uses "homme" for the whole person, man or woman. As in Colossians 3:9, the default says it inclusively and the traditional phrase is the alternative. Readable says "ce que nous étions avant", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: "esclave", "être esclave" at every level (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As the English: elsewhere French Balanced and Readable say "serviteur", but here slavery itself is the point, slavery to sin set against freedom from it, so "esclave" stays at every level.

decisions.choice: "종" for the slave and "종노릇 하다" for serving as a slave, at every level, through chapters 6-8
decisions.reason: As settled at 1:1 for the whole letter, the Korean uses "종" at every level. Korean "종" is itself a word for a person owned by a master, not a hired servant, so it keeps the hard edge the English keeps with "slave" in this chapter on slavery to sin and to righteousness; "종노릇 하다" makes the bondage explicit.

decisions.choice: "죄에서 벗어나 의롭다고 인정받았다" (L); "죄에서 풀려났다고 선언을 받았다" (B); "죄가 아무런 권리도 주장할 수 없다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one rendered "의롭다고 인정하다" through the letter; here it means being declared free from sin's claim (meaning decision). Literal keeps the letter's word with "벗어나" to show what the verdict is about; Balanced and Readable say the sense.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ἀπεθάνομεν σὺν Χριστῷ, πιστεύομεν ὅτι καὶ συζήσομεν αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: If now we died with Christ, we believe that also we will live with him;

en.L: Now if we died with {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, we believe that we will also live with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}};
en.B: Now if we died along with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, we believe we are also going to share in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life.
en.R: We died together with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Because of that, we believe we will live together with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} too.

es.L: Ahora bien, si morimos con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, creemos que también viviremos juntamente con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}};
es.B: Ahora bien, si morimos junto con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, creemos que también vamos a compartir {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida.
es.R: Morimos junto con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}. Por eso creemos que también viviremos con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Sasa kama tulikufa pamoja na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, tunaamini kuwa tutaishi pia pamoja na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}};
sw.B: Basi ikiwa tulikufa pamoja na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, tunaamini kwamba tutashiriki pia uzima {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Tulikufa pamoja na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Kwa sababu hiyo, tunaamini kwamba tutaishi pamoja na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} pia.

fr.L: Or si nous sommes morts avec {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, nous croyons que nous vivrons aussi avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ;
fr.B: Or si nous sommes morts avec le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, nous croyons que nous aurons aussi part à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie.
fr.R: Nous sommes morts avec le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. C’est pourquoi nous croyons que nous vivrons aussi avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

ko.L: 그런데 만일 우리가 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}와 함께 죽었다면, 우리는 또한 그분과 함께 살 것이라고 믿습니다.
ko.B: 우리가 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}와 함께 죽었다면, 그분의 생명에도 함께 참여하게 될 것이라고 우리는 믿습니다.
ko.R: 우리는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}와 함께 죽었습니다. 그러므로 우리는 그분과 함께 살게 될 것도 믿습니다.

decisions.choice: if: a condition taken as true
decisions.reason: Paul is not doubting that believers died with Christ; he has just said so (verses 3-6). The "if" sets out the ground for what follows.

decisions.choice: we will live with him: now and at the resurrection
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the future tense may point to life with Christ after the resurrection, or to the new life that follows now (verse 11, "living to God"). The words are left as a future.
Readable states the condition as a fact, because it is one Paul takes as true.
Balanced says "share in his life" for the single Greek verb "live with".

source.text: εἰδότες ὅτι Χριστὸς ἐγερθεὶς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὐκέτι ἀποθνῄσκει, θάνατος αὐτοῦ οὐκέτι κυριεύει·

records.literal_gloss: knowing that Christ having been raised out of dead [ones] no longer dies, death of him no longer rules;

en.L: knowing that {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, having been raised from [the] dead, no longer dies; death no longer rules over {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: For we know that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, once raised from the dead, does not die any more; death is no longer {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} master.
en.R: We know that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} was raised from the dead and cannot die again. Death has no power over {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} anymore.

es.L: sabiendo que {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, habiendo sido resucitado de entre [los] muertos, no muere más; la muerte ya no gobierna sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Porque sabemos que {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, una vez resucitado de entre los muertos, no vuelve a morir; la muerte ya no es dueña de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Sabemos que {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} fue resucitado de entre los muertos y no puede volver a morir. La muerte ya no tiene poder sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: tukijua kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, baada ya kufufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu, hafi tena; kifo hakina tena utawala juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Kwa maana tunajua kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kwa kuwa amefufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu, hatakufa tena; kifo si bwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} tena.
sw.R: Tunajua kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alifufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu, wala hawezi kufa tena. Kifo hakina nguvu juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} tena.

fr.L: sachant que {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, ressuscité d’entre [les] morts, ne meurt plus ; la mort ne règne plus sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Car nous savons que {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, une fois ressuscité d’entre les morts, ne meurt plus ; la mort n’est plus {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} maître.
fr.R: Nous savons que {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} a été ressuscité d’entre les morts et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne peut plus mourir. La mort n’a plus aucun pouvoir sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

ko.L: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나셨으므로 다시는 죽지 않으시고, 죽음이 더 이상 그분을 지배하지 못한다는 것을 [우리는] 압니다.
ko.B: 우리가 알듯이, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나셨으므로 다시는 죽지 않으십니다. 죽음은 더 이상 그분의 주인이 아닙니다.
ko.R: 우리는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나셔서 다시는 죽으실 수 없다는 것을 압니다. 죽음은 이제 그분께 아무런 힘도 쓰지 못합니다.

decisions.choice: death no longer rules over him
decisions.reason: Death is pictured as a ruler (5:14, 5:17). Christ was under its power when he died, but his resurrection was not a return to a life that ends in death again, as with Lazarus; it was victory over death itself.
kyrieuō, "be lord over", is rendered "master" so that the picture of a ruler is kept without sounding like a title of Christ.

decisions.choice: "[우리는] 압니다" (L): the participle as a main verb
decisions.reason: The Greek continues the sentence of verse 8 with a participle ("knowing"). Korean cannot hang a participle on the end of a finished sentence, so Literal makes it the main verb and brackets the subject.

source.text: ὃ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν, τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ· ὃ δὲ ζῇ, ζῇ τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: That which for he died, to the sin he died once for all; that which but he lives, he lives to the God.

en.L: For [the death] that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died to sin once for all; but [the life] that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives to God.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died to sin once and for all; and now that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives for God.
en.R: When {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died to sin's power once and for all. The life {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives now, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives for God.

es.L: Porque [la muerte] que murió, al pecado la murió una vez para siempre; pero [la vida] que vive, la vive para Dios.
es.B: Cuando murió, murió al pecado una vez y para siempre; y ahora que vive, vive para Dios.
es.R: Cuando {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió, murió al poder del pecado una vez y para siempre. La vida que ahora vive, la vive para Dios.

sw.L: Kwa maana [kifo] alichokufa, aliifia dhambi mara moja kwa daima; lakini [uzima] anaoishi, anamwishia Mungu.
sw.B: Alipokufa, aliifia dhambi mara moja kwa daima; na sasa kwa kuwa yu hai, anaishi kwa ajili ya Mungu.
sw.R: {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alipokufa, aliifia nguvu ya dhambi mara moja kwa daima. Maisha anayoishi sasa, anayaishi kwa ajili ya Mungu.

fr.L: Car quant à [la mort] qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a subie, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est mort au péché une fois pour toutes ; mais quant à [la vie] qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit pour Dieu.
fr.B: Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est mort, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est mort au péché une fois pour toutes ; et maintenant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit pour Dieu.
fr.R: Quand le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est mort, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est mort une fois pour toutes au pouvoir du péché. La vie qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit maintenant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la vit pour Dieu.

ko.L: 그분이 죽으신 [죽음]은 죄에 대하여 단 한 번에 죽으신 것이고, 그분이 사시는 [삶]은 하나님께 대하여 사시는 것입니다.
ko.B: 그분이 죽으신 것은 죄에 대해 단 한 번으로 영원히 죽으신 것이고, 이제 살아 계신 것은 하나님을 위해 사시는 것입니다.
ko.R: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 죽으셨을 때, 그분은 죄의 권세에 대해 단 한 번으로 영원히 죽으셨습니다. 이제 그분이 사시는 삶은 하나님을 위해 사시는 삶입니다.

decisions.choice: he died to sin: he was finished with sin's power
decisions.reason: Christ never sinned (2 Corinthians 5:21). He died to sin in that he came under its power, which brings death, and by his death he left that power behind for good. Sin has no more claim on him.

decisions.choice: once for all: one time, never to be repeated
decisions.reason: ephapax means both "once" and "once and for all time", as Hebrews uses it of Christ's sacrifice (Hebrews 7:27, 9:12, 10:10).

decisions.choice: lives to God: lives for God and in relation to him
decisions.reason: The dative "to God" matches "to sin": his life belongs wholly to God.
Readable says "sin's power" so that no reader thinks Christ himself sinned.

decisions.choice: anamwishia Mungu (L); anaishi kwa ajili ya Mungu (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Lives to God" means living for God and in relation to him (m3). "Anaishi kwa Mungu" could be read as "lives with God" or "by God". Literal uses the applied form "kumwishia Mungu" (to live for God), which pairs with "aliifia dhambi" (he died to sin) as the Greek pairs the two datives; Balanced and Readable say "kwa ajili ya Mungu" (for God). The same holds in 6:11.
French "vivre à Dieu" is not natural, while "mourir au péché" is; so the dative "to God" is "pour Dieu" at every level, which says that his life belongs wholly to God.

decisions.choice: "단 한 번에" (L); "단 한 번으로 영원히" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The adverb means once, never to be repeated (meaning decision). Balanced and Readable add "영원히" to say that the one time is final; Literal keeps the single word.

source.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς λογίζεσθε ἑαυτοὺς εἶναι νεκροὺς μὲν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ζῶντας δὲ τῷ θεῷ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: So also you consider yourselves to be dead indeed to the sin, living but to the God in Christ Jesus.

en.L: So also you, count yourselves to be dead to sin, but living to God in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.
en.B: In the same way, you also are to count yourselves as dead to sin, and as living for God in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.
en.R: In the same way, you must think of yourselves as dead to sin's power but alive for God, because you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

es.L: Así también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:considérense|consideraos}} a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos muertos al pecado, pero vivos para Dios en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}.
es.B: Del mismo modo, también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:deben considerarse|debéis consideraros}} muertos al pecado y vivos para Dios en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}.
es.R: Del mismo modo, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:deben verse|debéis veros}} como muertos para el poder del pecado, pero vivos para Dios, porque {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}.

sw.L: Kadhalika ninyi pia, jihesabuni wenyewe kuwa mmeifia dhambi, lakini mnamwishia Mungu katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo, ninyi pia mnapaswa kujihesabu kuwa mmeifia dhambi, na kuwa mko hai kwa ajili ya Mungu katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.
sw.R: Vivyo hivyo, mnapaswa kujiona kuwa mmeifia nguvu ya dhambi, lakini mko hai kwa ajili ya Mungu, kwa sababu ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.

fr.L: Ainsi vous aussi, comptez-vous comme morts au péché, mais vivants pour Dieu {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.
fr.B: De la même manière, vous aussi, tenez-vous pour morts au péché et vivants pour Dieu {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.
fr.R: De la même façon, vous devez vous considérer comme morts pour le pouvoir du péché, mais vivants pour Dieu, parce que vous appartenez au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus.

ko.L: 이와 같이 여러분도 자신을 죄에 대하여는 죽은 사람이요, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 안에서 하나님께 대하여는 살아 있는 사람으로 여기십시오.
ko.B: 이와 같이 여러분도 자신을 죄에 대해서는 죽은 사람으로, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 안에서 하나님을 위해서는 살아 있는 사람으로 여기십시오.
ko.R: 이와 같이 여러분도 자신을 죄의 권세에 대해서는 죽은 사람으로 여기십시오. 그리고 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수께 속해 있으므로 하나님을 위해 살아 있는 사람으로 여기십시오.

decisions.reason: logizesthe can be a statement ("you count") or a command ("count"). After "so also you" it is most naturally a command, and verses 12-13 go on with commands.

decisions.choice: count: reckon as true, put to the account
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of God counting faith as righteousness in chapter 4. Believers are to treat as true what God has done.
Many later manuscripts add "our Lord" at the end, probably from verse 23. Early witnesses do not have it, and the SBLGNT ends with "Christ Jesus". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.
The same English as chapter 4, so the link to God's counting is kept.

decisions.choice: because you belong to Christ Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable explains "in Christ Jesus", as Romans 9:1 and 12:5 do.

The verb means to reckon something as true (m2). "Contarse" in Spanish suggests being counted among a group, so Literal and Balanced use "considerarse", the ordinary verb for regarding oneself as something; Readable says "verse como" (see yourselves as).

The verb means to reckon as true, to put to the account (m2). "Kuhesabu" is the verb Swahili Romans uses for God counting faith as righteousness (chapter 4) and in "kuhesabiwa haki", so the link with the bookkeeping word is kept at Literal and Balanced. Readable says "kujiona" (to see oneself as).
Literal keeps the verb "compter" used for God counting faith as righteousness in chapter 4; Balanced says "se tenir pour", the natural French for regarding oneself as something.

decisions.choice: "여기다" at every level for this verb (as through chapter 4)
decisions.reason: This is the verb of 4:3-24, where God "counted" faith as righteousness; the meaning decision says it means to reckon as true. "여기다" keeps the link at every level, including Readable, where it is plain enough for new readers.

source.text: Μὴ οὖν βασιλευέτω ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θνητῷ ὑμῶν σώματι εἰς τὸ ὑπακούειν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις αὐτοῦ, μηδὲ παριστάνετε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα ἀδικίας τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ἀλλὰ παραστήσατε ἑαυτοὺς τῷ θεῷ ὡσεὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ζῶντας καὶ τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν ὅπλα δικαιοσύνης τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Not therefore let reign the sin in the mortal of you body for the to obey the desires of it, \v 13 neither present the members of you [as] weapons of unrighteousness to the sin, but present yourselves to the God as from dead [ones] living and the members of you [as] weapons of righteousness to the God.

en.L: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body, so that you obey its desires, \v 13 and do not present your members [as] weapons of unrighteousness to sin, but present yourselves to God as [people] living from [the] dead, and your members [as] weapons of righteousness to God.
en.B: So do not let sin reign as king in your mortal body, making you obey its desires. \v 13 Do not keep handing over the parts of your body to sin as weapons for wrongdoing. Instead, hand yourselves over to God, as people who were dead and are now alive, and hand over the parts of your body to God as weapons for righteousness.
en.R: So do not let sin rule like a king in your body, which will one day die. Do not let sin make you do whatever your body craves. \v 13 Do not give any part of your body to sin to use as a weapon for doing wrong. Instead, give yourselves to God, since you were dead and now you are alive. Give every part of your body to God to use as a weapon for righteousness.

es.L: Por tanto, no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que el pecado reine en {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo mortal, de modo que {{plural_you:obedezcan|obedezcáis}} a los deseos [del cuerpo], \v 13 ni {{plural_you:presenten|presentéis}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} miembros [como] armas de injusticia al pecado, sino {{plural_you:preséntense|presentaos}} a Dios como [personas] vivas de entre [los] muertos, y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} miembros [como] armas de justicia a Dios.
es.B: Así que no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que el pecado gobierne como rey en {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo mortal, haciéndo{{plural_you:les|os}} obedecer los deseos del cuerpo. \v 13 No {{plural_you:sigan|sigáis}} entregando al pecado las partes de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo como armas de injusticia. Al contrario, {{plural_you:entréguense|entregaos}} a Dios, como quienes estaban muertos y ahora viven, y {{plural_you:entreguen|entregad}} a Dios las partes de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo como armas de justicia.
es.R: Por eso, no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que el pecado mande como un rey en {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo, que un día morirá. No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que el pecado {{plural_you:los|os}} lleve a hacer todo lo que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo desea. \v 13 No {{plural_you:entreguen|entreguéis}} ninguna parte de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo al pecado, para que la use como arma de la injusticia. Al contrario, {{plural_you:entréguense|entregaos}} a Dios, porque antes {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} muertos y ahora {{plural_you:viven|vivís}}. {{plural_you:Entreguen|Entregad}} a Dios cada parte de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo, para que la use como arma de la justicia.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo msiiache dhambi itawale katika mwili wenu unaokufa, na hivyo mzitii tamaa za mwili huo, \v 13 wala msivikabidhi viungo vyenu kwa dhambi [viwe] silaha za udhalimu, bali jikabidhini kwa Mungu kama [watu] walio hai kutoka kwa wafu, na viungo vyenu [viwe] silaha za haki kwa Mungu.
sw.B: Basi msiiache dhambi itawale kama mfalme katika mwili wenu ambao utakufa, ikiwafanya mzitii tamaa za mwili huo. \v 13 Msiendelee kuikabidhi dhambi viungo vya mwili wenu viwe silaha za udhalimu. Badala yake, jikabidhini kwa Mungu, kama watu waliokuwa wamekufa na sasa wako hai, na mkabidhini Mungu viungo vya mwili wenu viwe silaha za haki.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo msiiache dhambi itawale kama mfalme katika mwili wenu, ambao siku moja utakufa. Msiiache dhambi iwafanye mtende kila kitu ambacho mwili wenu unatamani. \v 13 Msiipe dhambi sehemu yoyote ya mwili wenu iitumie kama silaha ya kutenda mabaya. Badala yake, jitoeni kwa Mungu, kwa kuwa mlikuwa wafu na sasa mko hai. Mpeni Mungu kila sehemu ya mwili wenu aitumie kama silaha ya kutenda haki.

fr.L: Que le péché ne règne donc pas dans votre corps mortel, de sorte que vous obéissiez à ses désirs, \v 13 et ne présentez pas vos membres [comme] armes d’injustice au péché, mais présentez-vous vous-mêmes à Dieu comme [des] vivants [revenus] d’entre [les] morts, et vos membres [comme] armes de justice à Dieu.
fr.B: Ne laissez donc pas le péché régner en roi dans votre corps mortel, en vous faisant obéir à ses désirs. \v 13 Ne continuez pas à livrer les parties de votre corps au péché comme des armes au service du mal. Livrez-vous plutôt vous-mêmes à Dieu, comme des gens qui étaient morts et qui sont maintenant vivants, et livrez à Dieu les parties de votre corps comme des armes au service de la justice.
fr.R: Alors ne laissez pas le péché régner comme un roi dans votre corps, qui mourra un jour. Ne laissez pas le péché vous faire faire tout ce dont votre corps a envie. \v 13 Ne donnez aucune partie de votre corps au péché pour qu’il s’en serve comme d’une arme pour faire le mal. Donnez-vous plutôt à Dieu, puisque vous étiez morts et que maintenant vous êtes vivants. Donnez chaque partie de votre corps à Dieu pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’en serve comme d’une arme pour la justice.

ko.L: 그러므로 죄가 여러분의 죽을 몸 안에서 왕 노릇 하여 여러분이 몸의 욕망에 순종하게 하지 마십시오. \v 13 또 여러분의 지체를 불의의 무기로 죄에게 내주지 마십시오. 오히려 여러분 자신을 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아난 사람으로 하나님께 드리고, 여러분의 지체를 의의 무기로 하나님께 드리십시오.
ko.B: 그러므로 죄가 여러분의 죽을 몸 안에서 왕처럼 다스리지 못하게 하여, 여러분이 몸의 욕망에 순종하는 일이 없게 하십시오. \v 13 여러분 몸의 어느 부분도 계속 죄에게 내주어 불의의 무기가 되게 하지 마십시오. 오히려 죽었다가 다시 살아난 사람으로서 여러분 자신을 하나님께 드리고, 여러분 몸의 각 부분을 의의 무기로 하나님께 드리십시오.
ko.R: 그러므로 언젠가 죽을 여러분의 몸을 죄가 왕처럼 다스리지 못하게 하십시오. 여러분의 몸이 원하는 대로 무엇이든 하게 만드는 죄에게 지지 마십시오. \v 13 여러분 몸의 어느 부분도 죄에게 내주어 나쁜 일을 하는 무기로 쓰이게 하지 마십시오. 오히려 여러분 자신을 하나님께 드리십시오. 여러분은 죽었다가 이제 살아난 사람들입니다. 그리고 여러분 몸의 모든 부분을 하나님께 드려서 의를 위한 무기로 쓰이게 하십시오.

decisions.reason: autou is neuter and goes with "body", not with sin. Sin rules by making people do what the mortal body craves.
The body is still mortal; the resurrection of the body is still to come (8:11, 8:23). That is why sin can still try to rule in it.
hoplon can mean a tool of any kind, but in Paul it means weapons (13:12; 2 Corinthians 6:7, 10:4). The picture of sin as a ruler who wages war and pays wages (verse 23) fits weapons.

decisions.choice: do not go on handing over (present); hand yourselves over (aorist)
decisions.reason: The first command is in the present tense and forbids a habit; the second is aorist and calls for a decisive act of handing oneself to God.

decisions.choice: members: the parts of the body
decisions.reason: The "members" are the body's parts and abilities, hands, feet, tongue and eyes, through which a person acts.
Balanced and Readable say "parts of your body" for "members", which today means members of a group.
Readable explains "mortal".
adikia is the opposite of righteousness. Balanced and Readable use plain words; Literal keeps "unrighteousness" so the contrast with "righteousness" shows.

decisions.choice: a los deseos [del cuerpo] (L); los deseos del cuerpo (B)
decisions.reason: "Its desires" are the body's desires (m1). In the ustedes form "sus deseos" would be read as "your desires", so Literal names the body in brackets and Balanced says it plainly.

As in 3:5, Spanish "injusticia" is both the plain word and the opposite of "justicia", so every level keeps the pair of weapons (armas de injusticia / armas de justicia), where English Balanced and Readable say "wrongdoing". "Armas" renders the weapons picture at every level (m3).

The verb is putting something at someone's disposal (m4), as weapons are handed to a commander (m3). "Kukabidhi" (to hand over into someone's charge) says this more exactly than "kutoa" (to give); Literal and Balanced use it here and in 6:16 and 6:19. Readable uses the everyday "kutoa" and "kupa".

In 3:5 Literal and Balanced said "kutokuwa na haki" to keep "haki" in both words. After "silaha za" that phrase is heavy, and "udhalimu" (injustice, wrongdoing) is the ordinary opposite of "haki", so the pair of weapons ("silaha za udhalimu" / "silaha za haki") still stands. Readable says "kutenda mabaya" / "kutenda haki". "Silaha" (weapons) is kept at every level (m3).
Literal keeps "injustice" so that the contrast with "justice" later in the verse shows, as the English Literal keeps "unrighteousness"; Balanced and Readable say "le mal".
French needs a subject for using the parts of the body as weapons; Readable names God, to whom they are given, and the pronoun carries the deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "지체" (L); "몸의 각 부분" (B, R); "무기" at every level
decisions.reason: "지체" is the exact word for the members of a body, but it is now mostly church language, so Balanced and Readable say "몸의 각 부분". The meaning decision weighs "weapons" against "tools"; the Korean follows its choice with "무기", and the footnote of the meaning decision gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: "왕 노릇 하다" (L); "왕처럼 다스리다" (B, R), as in 5:21
decisions.reason: The verb continues the picture of sin as a king from 5:14-21, where the Korean levels settled these forms.

source.text: ἁμαρτία γὰρ ὑμῶν οὐ κυριεύσει, οὐ γάρ ἐστε ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χάριν.

records.literal_gloss: Sin for of you not will rule, not for you are under law but under grace.

en.L: For sin will not rule over you, for you are not under [the] law but under grace.
en.B: Sin will not be lord over you, for you do not live under the law but under grace.
en.R: Sin will not have power over you, because you no longer live under the rule of the law. You live under the rule of God's grace.

es.L: Porque el pecado no {{plural_you:les|os}} dominará, pues no {{plural_you:están|estáis}} bajo [la] ley sino bajo [la] gracia.
es.B: El pecado no será {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} señor, porque no {{plural_you:viven|vivís}} bajo la ley, sino bajo la gracia.
es.R: El pecado no tendrá poder sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque ya no {{plural_you:viven|vivís}} bajo el dominio de la ley. {{plural_you:Viven|Vivís}} bajo el dominio de la gracia de Dios.

sw.L: Kwa maana dhambi haitatawala juu yenu, kwa sababu hamko chini ya sheria bali chini ya neema.
sw.B: Dhambi haitakuwa bwana wenu, kwa maana hamwishi chini ya sheria bali chini ya neema.
sw.R: Dhambi haitakuwa na nguvu juu yenu, kwa sababu hamwishi tena chini ya utawala wa sheria. Mnaishi chini ya utawala wa neema ya Mungu.

fr.L: Car le péché ne dominera pas sur vous, car vous n’êtes pas sous [la] Loi mais sous [la] grâce.
fr.B: Le péché ne sera pas votre maître, car vous ne vivez pas sous la Loi mais sous la grâce.
fr.R: Le péché n’aura pas de pouvoir sur vous, parce que vous ne vivez plus sous l’autorité de la Loi. Vous vivez sous l’autorité de la grâce de Dieu.

ko.L: 죄가 여러분을 지배하지 못할 것입니다. 여러분은 율법 아래 있지 않고 은혜 아래 있기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 죄는 여러분의 주인이 되지 못할 것입니다. 여러분은 율법 아래가 아니라 은혜 아래 살고 있기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 죄는 여러분을 다스리지 못할 것입니다. 여러분은 더 이상 율법의 다스림 아래 살지 않고, 하나님의 은혜의 다스림 아래 살기 때문입니다.

decisions.reason: The future is a promise, not a command: sin will not be master, and the reason follows.

decisions.choice: under law: under the law of Moses as the order one lives by
decisions.reason: To be "under" something is to live under its rule (3:19, Galatians 3:23-25, 4:4-5). The law is good (7:12), but it could not break sin's power; it made sin plain and even gave it opportunity (5:20, 7:8). Grace now rules instead (5:21).
Balanced keeps the sense of kyrieuō, "be lord over", which sets sin's claim against the Lord's (verse 23).
Readable explains "under".
French "seigneur" said of sin would sound strange; "maître" keeps the picture of a ruler, as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: "지배하다" (L); "주인이 되다" (B); "다스리다" (R) for the verb of verses 9 and 14
decisions.reason: This verb means to be lord or master over. Literal uses the plain "지배하다" in verses 9 and 14; Balanced says "주인" to keep the master-and-slave picture of the chapter; Readable uses the common "다스리다".

fr.R: Puisque ce n’est pas la Loi qui nous dirige, mais la grâce de Dieu, est-ce que cela veut dire que nous pouvons pécher ?

decisions.reason: Verse 1 asked about staying in sin (present tense). This question uses the aorist: may we commit sins, since the law no longer condemns us?

Readable names God as the giver of grace.
