records.literal_gloss: Not know you that to whom you present yourselves [as] slaves for obedience, slaves you are to whom you obey, whether of sin to death or of obedience to righteousness?

en.L: Do you not know that to whomever you present yourselves [as] slaves for obedience, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, whether of sin [leading] to death, or of obedience [leading] to righteousness?
en.B: Surely you know this: if you put yourselves at someone's disposal as slaves, ready to obey, then you belong as slaves to the one you obey. That master is either sin, bringing death, or obedience, bringing righteousness.
en.R: You know that if you give yourselves to someone and promise to obey, you become slaves of the one you obey. If you obey sin, you are its slaves, and that leads to death. If you choose obedience, you are its slaves, and that leads to righteousness.

es.L: ¿No {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que a quien {{plural_you:se presentan|os presentáis}} [como] esclavos para obediencia, de aquel a quien {{plural_you:obedecen|obedecéis}} {{plural_you:son|sois}} esclavos, ya sea del pecado [que lleva] a la muerte, o de la obediencia [que lleva] a la justicia?
es.B: Sin duda {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} esto: si {{plural_you:se ponen|os ponéis}} a disposición de alguien como esclavos, dispuestos a obedecer, {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} como esclavos a aquel a quien {{plural_you:obedecen|obedecéis}}. Ese amo es o el pecado, que trae la muerte, o la obediencia, que trae la justicia.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} que, si {{plural_you:se entregan|os entregáis}} a alguien y {{plural_you:prometen|prometéis}} obedecerle, {{plural_you:se hacen|os hacéis}} esclavos de aquel a quien {{plural_you:obedecen|obedecéis}}. Si {{plural_you:obedecen|obedecéis}} al pecado, {{plural_you:son|sois}} sus esclavos, y eso lleva a la muerte. Si {{plural_you:eligen|elegís}} la obediencia, {{plural_you:son|sois}} sus esclavos, y eso lleva a la justicia.

sw.L: Je, hamjui kwamba mkijikabidhi kwa mtu [kama] watumwa ili mumtii, ninyi ni watumwa wa yule mnayemtii, iwe ni wa dhambi [inayoelekeza] kwenye kifo, au wa utii [unaoelekeza] kwenye haki?
sw.B: Hakika mnajua jambo hili: mkijiweka chini ya mtu kama watumwa, tayari kumtii, basi ninyi ni watumwa wa yule mnayemtii. Bwana huyo ni dhambi, inayoleta kifo, au ni utii, unaoleta haki.
sw.R: Mnajua kwamba mkijitoa kwa mtu na kuahidi kumtii, mnakuwa watumwa wa yule mnayemtii. Mkiitii dhambi, ninyi ni watumwa wake, na hilo linaleta kifo. Mkichagua utii, ninyi ni watumwa wake, na hilo linaleta haki.

fr.L: Ne savez-vous pas que si vous vous présentez à quelqu’un [comme] esclaves pour [lui] obéir, vous êtes esclaves de celui à qui vous obéissez, soit du péché [qui mène] à la mort, soit de l’obéissance [qui mène] à la justice ?
fr.B: Vous le savez bien : si vous vous mettez à la disposition de quelqu’un comme esclaves, prêts à obéir, vous appartenez comme esclaves à celui à qui vous obéissez. Ce maître, c’est soit le péché, qui mène à la mort, soit l’obéissance, qui mène à la justice.
fr.R: Vous savez que si vous vous donnez à quelqu’un en promettant de lui obéir, vous devenez les esclaves de celui à qui vous obéissez. Si vous obéissez au péché, vous êtes ses esclaves, et cela mène à la mort. Si vous choisissez l’obéissance, vous êtes esclaves de l’obéissance, et cela mène à la justice.

ko.L: 여러분이 누구에게 순종하려고 자신을 종으로 내주면, 여러분은 순종하는 그 대상의 종이 된다는 것을 알지 못합니까? 죽음에 [이르는] 죄의 [종]이든지, 의에 [이르는] 순종의 [종]이든지 말입니다.
ko.B: 여러분도 알고 있지 않습니까? 여러분이 누군가에게 자신을 종으로 내주어 순종하면, 여러분은 순종하는 그 주인의 종이 됩니다. 그 주인은 죽음에 이르게 하는 죄이거나, 의에 이르게 하는 순종입니다.
ko.R: 여러분은 알고 있습니다. 여러분이 누군가에게 자신을 내주고 순종하기로 하면, 여러분은 순종하는 그 주인의 종이 됩니다. 죄에게 순종하면 죄의 종이 되고, 그 길은 죽음으로 이어집니다. 순종을 택하면 순종의 종이 되고, 그 길은 의로 이어집니다.

decisions.reason: In the Roman world a free person could sell himself or herself into slavery, for instance to pay a debt. Whoever did so belonged to the master and had to obey.

decisions.choice: obedience leading to righteousness: a right life now and God's verdict at the end
decisions.reason: Set against "death", righteousness here is the outcome of obeying: a life that is right with God, ending in his final verdict of acquittal and life (verses 22-23). It is not earned by obedience; the obedience is the obedience of faith (1:5).
Balanced turns the question into a statement, since Paul expects the answer yes.

decisions.choice: That master is (B); If you obey sin / If you choose obedience (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek names the two masters in a short phrase; Balanced and Readable supply the words that link them back to "slaves".
"Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery itself is the point: slavery to sin set against obedience; the whole passage turns on whose slave one is.

decisions.choice: "여러분도 알고 있지 않습니까?" as its own question (B); a statement "여러분은 알고 있습니다" (R)
decisions.reason: Korean puts "do you not know" at the end of what is known, which would bury it after the long relative clause. Balanced asks it first as a short question and then gives the content; Readable makes it a plain statement, as the English Readable does.

source.text: χάρις δὲ τῷ θεῷ ὅτι ἦτε δοῦλοι τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὑπηκούσατε δὲ ἐκ καρδίας εἰς ὃν παρεδόθητε τύπον διδαχῆς, ἐλευθερωθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐδουλώθητε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ·

records.literal_gloss: Thanks but to the God that you were slaves of the sin, you obeyed but from heart to which you were handed over form of teaching, \v 18 having been set free and from the sin, you were enslaved to the righteousness;

en.L: But thanks [be] to God that you were slaves of sin, but you obeyed from [the] heart the pattern of teaching to which you were handed over, \v 18 and having been set free from sin, you were enslaved to righteousness.
en.B: But God be thanked! Once you were slaves of sin, yet you gave wholehearted obedience to the pattern of teaching into whose care you were handed. \v 18 Freed from sin, you were made slaves of righteousness.
en.R: But thank God! You were once slaves of sin. But then you obeyed with all your heart the teaching God placed you under. \v 18 You were set free from sin, and now you are slaves of righteousness.

es.L: Pero gracias [sean dadas] a Dios, porque {{plural_you:eran|erais}} esclavos del pecado, pero {{plural_you:obedecieron|obedecisteis}} de corazón al modelo de enseñanza al que {{plural_you:fueron entregados|fuisteis entregados}}, \v 18 y, liberados del pecado, {{plural_you:fueron hechos|fuisteis hechos}} esclavos de la justicia.
es.B: ¡Pero demos gracias a Dios! Antes {{plural_you:eran|erais}} esclavos del pecado, pero {{plural_you:obedecieron|obedecisteis}} de todo corazón al modelo de enseñanza a cuyo cuidado {{plural_you:fueron confiados|fuisteis confiados}}. \v 18 Liberados del pecado, {{plural_you:llegaron|llegasteis}} a ser esclavos de la justicia.
es.R: ¡Pero gracias a Dios! Antes {{plural_you:eran|erais}} esclavos del pecado. Pero luego {{plural_you:obedecieron|obedecisteis}} de todo corazón la enseñanza bajo la cual Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} puso. \v 18 {{plural_you:Fueron liberados|Fuisteis liberados}} del pecado, y ahora {{plural_you:son|sois}} esclavos de la justicia.

sw.L: Lakini shukrani [ziwe] kwa Mungu kwamba mlikuwa watumwa wa dhambi, lakini mkatii kutoka moyoni kielelezo cha mafundisho ambacho mlikabidhiwa kwacho, \v 18 na baada ya kuachiliwa huru kutoka kwa dhambi, mkageuzwa kuwa watumwa wa haki.
sw.B: Lakini Mungu ashukuriwe! Zamani mlikuwa watumwa wa dhambi, lakini mkatii kwa moyo wote kielelezo cha mafundisho ambacho mlikabidhiwa kwacho ili kiwatunze. \v 18 Mkiwa mmeachiliwa kutoka kwa dhambi, mkawa watumwa wa haki.
sw.R: Lakini tumshukuru Mungu! Zamani mlikuwa watumwa wa dhambi. Lakini kisha mkayatii kwa moyo wote mafundisho ambayo Mungu aliwakabidhi myafuate. \v 18 Mliwekwa huru kutoka kwa dhambi, na sasa ninyi ni watumwa wa haki.

fr.L: Mais grâces [soient rendues] à Dieu de ce que vous étiez esclaves du péché, mais [que] vous avez obéi de [tout] cœur au modèle d’enseignement auquel vous avez été livrés, \v 18 et, ayant été libérés du péché, vous avez été rendus esclaves de la justice.
fr.B: Mais Dieu soit remercié ! Autrefois vous étiez esclaves du péché, mais vous avez obéi de tout votre cœur au modèle d’enseignement entre les mains duquel vous avez été remis. \v 18 Libérés du péché, vous êtes devenus esclaves de la justice.
fr.R: Mais merci à Dieu ! Avant, vous étiez esclaves du péché. Mais ensuite, vous avez obéi de tout votre cœur à l’enseignement sous lequel Dieu vous a placés. \v 18 Vous avez été libérés du péché, et maintenant vous êtes esclaves de la justice.

ko.L: 그러나 하나님께 감사[드립니다]. 여러분은 죄의 종이었으나, 여러분이 넘겨진 가르침의 본을 마음으로부터 순종하였고, \v 18 죄에서 해방되어 의에게 종이 되었습니다.
ko.B: 그러나 하나님께 감사드립니다! 여러분은 전에 죄의 종이었지만, 여러분을 맡긴 가르침의 본에 온 마음으로 순종했습니다. \v 18 그리고 죄에서 해방되어 의의 종이 되었습니다.
ko.R: 그러나 하나님께 감사드립니다! 여러분은 전에 죄의 종이었습니다. 그러나 하나님께서 여러분을 맡기신 가르침에 여러분은 온 마음으로 순종했습니다. \v 18 여러분은 죄에서 해방되었고, 이제는 의의 종이 되었습니다.

decisions.reason: charis here is thanks given to God, as in 7:25 and 1 Corinthians 15:57, not grace given by him.

decisions.choice: thanks that, though you were slaves of sin, you obeyed
decisions.reason: Paul is not thankful that they were slaves of sin. The two clauses go together: thanks be to God that they were slaves of sin but obeyed.

decisions.choice: handed over to the pattern of teaching
decisions.reason: One would expect "the teaching handed over to you" (as in 1 Corinthians 15:3). Paul turns it round: they were handed over to the teaching, like slaves passed to a new master. The "pattern" (typos) is the shape of the gospel teaching that now forms their lives. The passive implies that God handed them over.
The aorist passive "you were enslaved" describes what happened when they were freed from sin: no one is without a master, and their new master is righteousness.
Balanced uses an exclamation for the short Greek thanksgiving.

decisions.choice: the teaching God placed you under
alternatives: the teaching to which you were handed over
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who handed them over, which the passive implies.

decisions.choice: gracias [sean dadas] a Dios (L); ¡Pero demos gracias a Dios! (B); ¡Pero gracias a Dios! (R)
decisions.reason: The word that is "grace" elsewhere means thanks here (m1). Spanish "gracias" is the same word family as "gracia", so the Greek link can still be heard. Balanced says "demos gracias" (let us give thanks) so that it is not heard as the casual "¡gracias a Dios!" (thank goodness), as the English Balanced says "God be thanked".
The word is a pattern or mould that shapes those handed over to it (m3). "Modelo" says this; "forma de doctrina" reads as a set form of dogma.

decisions.choice: shukrani [ziwe] kwa Mungu (L); Mungu ashukuriwe! (B); tumshukuru Mungu! (R)
decisions.reason: The word that is "grace" elsewhere means thanks here (m1). Swahili has no word that covers both, and "neema" would read as grace, so every level says thanks.

decisions.choice: kielelezo cha mafundisho ambacho mlikabidhiwa kwacho
decisions.reason: The readers were handed over to the teaching, not the teaching to them (m3). "Mliyokabidhiwa" alone would mean "the teaching entrusted to you"; "mlikabidhiwa kwacho" (you were entrusted to it) keeps the direction of the Greek.
"Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery itself is the point: slaves of sin set against being freed from sin.

The Greek word is the one translated "grace" elsewhere, used here for thanks to God (see the meaning decision). French "rendre grâces" says thanks with the same word, so Literal keeps the link; Balanced and Readable say it in everyday French.

decisions.choice: "여러분이 넘겨진 가르침의 본" (L); "여러분을 맡긴 가르침의 본" (B); "하나님께서 여러분을 맡기신 가르침" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says the readers were handed over to the teaching, not the teaching to them. Literal keeps "넘겨지다", the verb of 1:24 and 4:25; Balanced says "맡기다" (entrusted into its care); Readable names God as the one who did it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἀνθρώπινον λέγω διὰ τὴν ἀσθένειαν τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν· ὥσπερ γὰρ παρεστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ καὶ τῇ ἀνομίᾳ εἰς τὴν ἀνομίαν, οὕτως νῦν παραστήσατε τὰ μέλη ὑμῶν δοῦλα τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ εἰς ἁγιασμόν.

records.literal_gloss: Human I speak because of the weakness of the flesh of you; just as for you presented the members of you slaves to the impurity and to the lawlessness for the lawlessness, so now present the members of you slaves to the righteousness for sanctification.

en.L: I speak in human [terms] because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you presented your members [as] slaves to impurity and to lawlessness, [leading] to lawlessness, so now present your members [as] slaves to righteousness, [leading] to sanctification.
en.B: I am putting this in everyday human terms because of your natural human weakness. Just as you once handed over the parts of your body as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness, which only led to more lawlessness, so now hand them over as slaves to righteousness, leading to holiness.
en.R: I am using a picture from everyday life because you are only human and these things are hard to grasp. You used to give the parts of your body as slaves to impure living and to lawless living, and the lawlessness kept growing. Now give them as slaves to righteousness, so that you will become holy.

es.L: Hablo en [términos] humanos a causa de la debilidad de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} carne. Porque así como {{plural_you:presentaron|presentasteis}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} miembros [como] esclavos a la impureza y a la iniquidad, [que lleva] a la iniquidad, así ahora {{plural_you:presenten|presentad}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} miembros [como] esclavos a la justicia, [que lleva] a la santificación.
es.B: Estoy hablando en términos humanos, de la vida diaria, a causa de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} natural debilidad humana. Así como antes {{plural_you:entregaron|entregasteis}} las partes de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo como esclavas a la impureza y a la iniquidad, lo que solo llevó a más iniquidad, así ahora {{plural_you:entréguenlas|entregadlas}} como esclavas a la justicia, para llegar a la santidad.
es.R: Uso un ejemplo de la vida diaria porque {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} solo humanos y estas cosas son difíciles de entender. Antes {{plural_you:entregaban|entregabais}} las partes de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo como esclavas a una vida impura y sin ley, y {{plural_you:vivían|vivíais}} cada vez más sin ley. Ahora {{plural_you:entréguenlas|entregadlas}} como esclavas a la justicia, para que {{plural_you:lleguen|lleguéis}} a ser santos.

sw.L: Ninazungumza kwa lugha ya kibinadamu kwa sababu ya udhaifu wa mwili wenu. Kwa maana kama vile mlivyovikabidhi viungo vyenu [viwe] watumwa wa uchafu na wa uasi, [unaoelekeza] kwenye uasi, vivyo hivyo sasa vikabidhini viungo vyenu [viwe] watumwa wa haki, [inayoelekeza] kwenye utakaso.
sw.B: Ninasema hivi kwa lugha ya kila siku ya kibinadamu kwa sababu ya udhaifu wenu wa kibinadamu. Kama vile zamani mlivyovikabidhi viungo vya mwili wenu viwe watumwa wa uchafu na wa uasi, jambo lililoleta uasi zaidi tu, vivyo hivyo sasa vikabidhini viwe watumwa wa haki, ili kuleta utakatifu.
sw.R: Ninatumia mfano wa maisha ya kila siku kwa sababu ninyi ni wanadamu tu, na mambo haya ni magumu kuelewa. Zamani mlitoa sehemu za mwili wenu ziwe watumwa wa maisha machafu na ya uasi, na uasi wenu ukazidi kukua. Sasa zitoeni ziwe watumwa wa haki, ili mpate kuwa watakatifu.

fr.L: Je parle à la manière humaine à cause de la faiblesse de votre chair. Car, de même que vous avez présenté vos membres [comme] esclaves à l’impureté et à l’iniquité, pour l’iniquité, de même présentez maintenant vos membres [comme] esclaves à la justice, pour la sanctification.
fr.B: Je m’exprime en termes humains, ordinaires, à cause de votre faiblesse humaine. De même qu’autrefois vous avez livré les parties de votre corps comme esclaves à l’impureté et au mépris de la loi, ce qui ne menait qu’à plus de mépris de la loi, livrez-les maintenant comme esclaves à la justice, ce qui mène à la sainteté.
fr.R: J’utilise une image de la vie de tous les jours, parce que vous êtes humains et que ces choses sont difficiles à comprendre. Avant, vous donniez les parties de votre corps comme esclaves à une vie impure et à une vie sans loi, et le désordre ne faisait que grandir. Maintenant, donnez-les comme esclaves à la justice, pour que vous deveniez saints.

ko.L: 여러분의 육신의 연약함 때문에 나는 사람의 [방식으로] 말합니다. 여러분이 전에 여러분의 지체를 더러움과 불법에 종으로 내주어 불법에 [이르렀던] 것과 같이, 이제는 여러분의 지체를 의에 종으로 내주어 거룩함에 [이르십시오].
ko.B: 여러분이 사람으로서 연약하기 때문에, 나는 일상에서 쓰는 말로 이야기합니다. 여러분이 전에 몸의 각 부분을 더러움과 불법에 종으로 내주어 불법이 더욱 늘어났던 것처럼, 이제는 몸의 각 부분을 의에 종으로 내주어 거룩함에 이르십시오.
ko.R: 여러분은 사람일 뿐이어서 이런 일들을 깨닫기 어렵습니다. 그래서 나는 일상생활의 예를 들어 말합니다. 여러분은 전에 몸의 각 부분을 더러운 생활과 법을 무시하는 생활에 종으로 내주었고, 그래서 불법이 점점 더 늘어났습니다. 이제는 몸의 각 부분을 의에 종으로 내주십시오. 그러면 여러분은 거룩한 사람이 될 것입니다.

decisions.choice: I speak in human terms: I use an everyday picture
decisions.reason: Paul apologizes for the picture of slavery. Being "slaves of righteousness" is not the whole truth about life with God, which is freedom (8:15, 8:21), but the picture helps.

decisions.choice: the weakness of your flesh: human limitation
decisions.reason: Flesh here is human nature in its weakness. The weakness may be of understanding, so that a plain picture is needed, or of moral strength, so that a strong one is needed. Either way it is ordinary human frailty, not the flesh set against the Spirit as in chapter 8.
hagiasmos is the process or state of being set apart to God and made holy. It is the outcome of serving righteousness, as death is the outcome of sin (verses 21-22).

decisions.choice: natural human weakness (B); you are only human (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "flesh" means here, plain human frailty, instead of "flesh", which in Romans often means human nature under sin.
Balanced and Readable use everyday words for hagiasmos; Literal keeps "sanctification".

decisions.choice: natural debilidad humana (B); son solo humanos (R)
decisions.reason: Here "flesh" means plain human limitation (m2), not human nature set against the Spirit, so Readable does not say "yo pecador" as Galatians 5 and Romans 13:14 do. Literal keeps "carne"; Balanced and Readable say what the English says.

Literal keeps "santificación". The word means being made holy (m3), and Balanced and Readable say "santidad" and "llegar a ser santos", as the English says "holiness" and "become holy". The same in 6:22.
The word is life without regard to God's law. "Iniquidad" is the established Spanish word for it; "anarquía" would sound political. Readable says "sin ley" (lawless).

decisions.choice: udhaifu wenu wa kibinadamu (B); ninyi ni wanadamu tu (R)
decisions.reason: Here "flesh" means plain human limitation (m2), not human nature set against the Spirit, so Balanced and Readable do not say "asili ya dhambi". Literal keeps "mwili", as the style guide does for plain human life.
The word means being made holy (m3). Literal says "utakaso" (sanctification, the process); Balanced "utakatifu" (holiness) and Readable "become holy", as the English does. The same in 6:22.
"Uasi" (rebellion, lawlessness) is the usual Swahili word for living in defiance of God's law; "uvunjaji wa sheria" (law-breaking) sounds like a matter for the police.
"Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery itself is the point: slavery to impurity set against slavery to righteousness, in the passage on freedom from sin.

decisions.choice: "l'iniquité" (L); "le mépris de la loi" (B); "une vie sans loi", "le désordre" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "lawlessness", living as if there were no law. Literal uses the traditional single word "iniquité"; Balanced and Readable spell out the link with law, in lower case, since any law is meant, not only the law of Moses.

decisions.choice: "육신" (L) for the flesh, as through the letter; "사람으로서 연약하다" (B); "사람일 뿐" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "육신", the word for flesh through the letter (1:3; 4:1). Here the meaning decision reads it as plain human limitation, so Balanced and Readable say that sense.

decisions.choice: "거룩함" (L, B); "거룩한 사람이 되다" (R) for sanctification, here and in verse 22
decisions.reason: The noun means being made holy (meaning decision). "성화" is a theological term that new readers do not know; "거룩함에 이르다" says the process plainly.

source.text: Ὅτε γὰρ δοῦλοι ἦτε τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ἐλεύθεροι ἦτε τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ.

records.literal_gloss: When for slaves you were of the sin, free you were to the righteousness.

en.L: For when you were slaves of sin, you were free with regard to righteousness.
en.B: Back when sin owned you as slaves, you were free, as far as righteousness was concerned.
en.R: When you were slaves of sin, you did not have to answer to righteousness at all.

es.L: Porque cuando {{plural_you:eran|erais}} esclavos del pecado, respecto de la justicia {{plural_you:eran|erais}} libres.
es.B: Cuando el pecado {{plural_you:los|os}} tenía como esclavos, {{plural_you:eran|erais}} libres en lo que toca a la justicia.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:eran|erais}} esclavos del pecado, no {{plural_you:tenían|teníais}} que rendir cuentas a la justicia para nada.

sw.L: Kwa maana wakati mlipokuwa watumwa wa dhambi, mlikuwa huru kwa upande wa haki.
sw.B: Zamani dhambi ilipowamiliki kama watumwa, mlikuwa huru, kwa kadiri haki inavyohusika.
sw.R: Mlipokuwa watumwa wa dhambi, hamkuwajibika hata kidogo kwa haki.

fr.L: Car lorsque vous étiez esclaves du péché, vous étiez libres à l’égard de la justice.
fr.B: Au temps où le péché vous possédait comme esclaves, vous étiez libres, pour ce qui est de la justice.
fr.R: Quand vous étiez esclaves du péché, vous n’aviez aucun compte à rendre à la justice.

ko.L: 여러분이 죄의 종이었을 때에는 의에 대하여 자유로웠습니다.
ko.B: 여러분이 죄의 종이었을 때에는, 의에 관해서는 자유로운 사람들이었습니다.
ko.R: 여러분이 죄의 종이었을 때에는 의에 대해 아무런 책임도 지지 않았습니다.

decisions.choice: free with regard to righteousness: righteousness was not their master
decisions.reason: The dative means "free as far as righteousness goes". The freedom was no real freedom: it was the freedom of slaves who did not serve righteousness, and its end was death (verse 21).

decisions.choice: did not have to answer to
decisions.reason: Readable explains the irony of "free" in plain words.
"Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery itself is the point: slaves of sin, "free" from righteousness.
The meaning decision says that righteousness was not their master. "자유로웠다" alone could sound like praise to a new reader, so Readable says they did not answer to righteousness.

source.text: τίνα οὖν καρπὸν εἴχετε τότε ἐφ’ οἷς νῦν ἐπαισχύνεσθε;

records.literal_gloss: What therefore fruit had you then in the [things] of which now you are ashamed?

en.L: What fruit then did you have at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed?
en.B: So what fruit did you get back then from the things that now make you ashamed?
en.R: What good did you get back then from doing the things that now make you ashamed?

es.L: ¿Qué fruto, pues, {{plural_you:tenían|teníais}} entonces de las cosas de las que ahora {{plural_you:se avergüenzan|os avergonzáis}}?
es.B: Entonces, ¿qué fruto {{plural_you:sacaron|sacasteis}} en aquel tiempo de las cosas que ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} avergüenzan?
es.R: ¿Qué bien {{plural_you:sacaron|sacasteis}} en aquel tiempo de hacer las cosas que ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} dan vergüenza?

sw.L: Basi mlikuwa na tunda gani wakati ule kutokana na mambo ambayo sasa mnayaonea aibu?
sw.B: Basi, mlipata tunda gani wakati ule kutokana na mambo ambayo sasa yanawatia aibu?
sw.R: Mlipata faida gani wakati ule kwa kutenda mambo ambayo sasa yanawaaibisha?

fr.L: Quel fruit aviez-vous donc alors des choses dont vous avez maintenant honte ?
fr.B: Quel fruit avez-vous donc retiré, à l’époque, de ces choses qui vous font honte maintenant ?
fr.R: Qu’est-ce que cela vous a apporté de bon, à l’époque, de faire ces choses qui vous font honte maintenant ?

ko.L: 그러면 그때 여러분은 지금 부끄러워하는 그 일들에서 무슨 열매를 얻었습니까?
ko.B: 그렇다면 여러분은 지금 부끄럽게 여기는 그 일들로 그때 무슨 열매를 얻었습니까?
ko.R: 여러분은 지금 부끄럽게 여기는 그 일들을 하면서, 그때 무슨 좋은 것을 얻었습니까?

decisions.choice: one question: what fruit came from the things you are now ashamed of
alternatives: What fruit did you have then? Things you are now ashamed of.
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads the whole verse up to here as one question. Some read the question as ending after "then", with the answer "things you are now ashamed of". The sense is much the same.
Fruit is what a life produces. Verse 22 takes up the same word for the life given to God.
Readable says what "fruit" means here.

source.text: τὸ γὰρ τέλος ἐκείνων θάνατος·

records.literal_gloss: The for end of those [things] [is] death.

en.L: For the end of those things [is] death.
en.B: Those things end in death.
en.R: In the end, those things bring death.

es.L: Porque el fin de aquellas cosas [es la] muerte.
es.B: Esas cosas terminan en la muerte.
es.R: Al final, esas cosas traen la muerte.

sw.L: Kwa maana mambo hayo mwisho wake [ni] kifo.
sw.B: Mambo hayo huishia katika kifo.
sw.R: Mwishowe, mambo hayo huleta kifo.

fr.L: Car la fin de ces choses, [c’est] la mort.
fr.B: Ces choses aboutissent à la mort.
fr.R: Au bout du compte, ces choses amènent la mort.

ko.L: 그 일들의 끝은 죽음이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그런 일들은 결국 죽음으로 끝납니다.
ko.R: 결국 그런 일들은 죽음을 가져옵니다.

decisions.choice: end: the goal and final outcome
decisions.reason: telos is the point a thing comes to, its result. Death is not only a penalty added from outside but where that way of life leads (verse 23).

alternatives: The end of those things is death.
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the noun "end" into a verb.

source.text: νυνὶ δέ, ἐλευθερωθέντες ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας δουλωθέντες δὲ τῷ θεῷ, ἔχετε τὸν καρπὸν ὑμῶν εἰς ἁγιασμόν, τὸ δὲ τέλος ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

records.literal_gloss: Now but, having been set free from the sin, having been enslaved but to the God, you have the fruit of you to sanctification, the and end life eternal.

en.L: But now, having been set free from sin and having been enslaved to God, you have your fruit [leading] to sanctification, and the end [is] eternal life.
en.B: Now, though, freed from sin and made slaves of God, you have fruit that leads to holiness, and its outcome is eternal life.
en.R: But now you have been set free from sin, and you have become God's slaves. What you get from this is a holy life, and in the end you will have eternal life.

es.L: Pero ahora, liberados del pecado y hechos esclavos de Dios, {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} fruto [que lleva] a la santificación, y el fin [es la] vida eterna.
es.B: Pero ahora, libres del pecado y hechos esclavos de Dios, {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} un fruto que lleva a la santidad, y su resultado final es la vida eterna.
es.R: Pero ahora {{plural_you:han|habéis}} sido liberados del pecado, y {{plural_you:se han hecho|os habéis hecho}} esclavos de Dios. Lo que {{plural_you:ganan|ganáis}} con esto es una vida santa, y al final {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} la vida eterna.

sw.L: Lakini sasa, mkiwa mmeachiliwa kutoka kwa dhambi na kufanywa watumwa wa Mungu, mna tunda lenu [linaloelekeza] kwenye utakaso, na mwisho [ni] uzima wa milele.
sw.B: Sasa, hata hivyo, mkiwa huru kutoka kwa dhambi na mmefanywa watumwa wa Mungu, mna tunda linaloleta utakatifu, na matokeo yake ni uzima wa milele.
sw.R: Lakini sasa mmewekwa huru kutoka kwa dhambi, na mmekuwa watumwa wa Mungu. Mnachopata kutokana na hili ni maisha matakatifu, na mwishowe mtakuwa na uzima wa milele.

fr.L: Mais maintenant, ayant été libérés du péché et rendus esclaves de Dieu, vous avez votre fruit pour la sanctification, et la fin, [c’est] la vie éternelle.
fr.B: Mais maintenant, libérés du péché et devenus esclaves de Dieu, vous portez un fruit qui mène à la sainteté, et son aboutissement est la vie éternelle.
fr.R: Mais maintenant, vous avez été libérés du péché, et vous êtes devenus les esclaves de Dieu. Ce que vous y gagnez, c’est une vie sainte, et à la fin, vous aurez la vie éternelle.

ko.L: 그러나 이제는 여러분이 죄에서 해방되고 하나님께 종이 되어, 거룩함에 [이르는] 여러분의 열매를 얻고 있으니, 그 끝은 영원한 생명입니다.
ko.B: 그러나 이제 여러분은 죄에서 해방되어 하나님의 종이 되었으니, 거룩함에 이르는 열매를 맺고 있습니다. 그 결과는 영원한 생명입니다.
ko.R: 그러나 이제 여러분은 죄에서 해방되었고, 하나님의 종이 되었습니다. 그 결과로 여러분은 거룩한 삶을 살게 되었고, 마지막에는 영원한 생명을 얻을 것입니다.

decisions.choice: but now: the new situation since they believed
decisions.reason: "But now" sets the present against "then" in verse 21, as in 3:21 and 7:6.

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: Eternal life is the life of God's new age, without end, given in full at the resurrection (2:7, 5:21).
As in verse 19.
Readable says what "fruit" means here.
"Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery itself is the point: freed from sin and made slaves of God: the contrast with freedom is the point.

source.text: τὰ γὰρ ὀψώνια τῆς ἁμαρτίας θάνατος, τὸ δὲ χάρισμα τοῦ θεοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιος ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: The for wages of the sin [is] death, the but gift of the God [is] life eternal in Christ Jesus the Lord of us.

en.L: For the wages of sin [is] death, but the gift of God [is] eternal life in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus our Lord.
en.B: The wages sin pays are death, but God's free gift is eternal life in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our Lord.
en.R: Sin pays out death as its wages. But God gives eternal life as a free gift to everyone who belongs to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus our Lord.

es.L: Porque el salario del pecado [es] muerte, pero el don de Dios [es] vida eterna en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}, nuestro Señor.
es.B: El salario que paga el pecado es la muerte, pero el don que Dios da gratis es la vida eterna en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}, nuestro Señor.
es.R: El pecado paga con la muerte, como si fuera un sueldo. Pero Dios da la vida eterna como regalo a todos los que pertenecen {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}, nuestro Señor.

sw.L: Kwa maana ujira wa dhambi [ni] kifo, lakini zawadi ya Mungu [ni] uzima wa milele katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu Bwana wetu.
sw.B: Ujira ambao dhambi hulipa ni kifo, lakini zawadi ya bure ya Mungu ni uzima wa milele katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu Bwana wetu.
sw.R: Dhambi hulipa kifo kama ujira wake. Lakini Mungu hutoa uzima wa milele kama zawadi ya bure kwa kila mtu aliye wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu Bwana wetu.

fr.L: Car le salaire du péché, [c’est] la mort, mais le don gratuit de Dieu, [c’est] la vie éternelle {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus notre Seigneur.
fr.B: Le salaire que paie le péché, c’est la mort, mais le don gratuit de Dieu, c’est la vie éternelle {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, notre Seigneur.
fr.R: Le péché paie un salaire : la mort. Mais Dieu donne la vie éternelle comme un cadeau à tous ceux qui appartiennent au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, notre Seigneur.

ko.L: 죄의 삯은 죽음이지만, 하나님의 은사는 우리 주 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 안에서 [얻는] 영원한 생명이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 죄가 주는 품삯은 죽음이지만, 하나님께서 거저 주시는 선물은 우리 주 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 안에 있는 영원한 생명입니다.
ko.R: 죄는 그 품삯으로 죽음을 줍니다. 그러나 하나님께서는 우리 주 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수께 속한 모든 사람에게 영원한 생명을 선물로 거저 주십니다.

decisions.reason: opsōnion was the pay or ration money of a soldier, and then any wage. It fits the picture of sin as a ruler with weapons at its service (verse 13). Sin pays what is earned; God gives what is not earned.
charisma is a gift given freely, out of grace (5:15-16). It stands against wages, which are owed.

decisions.choice: in Christ Jesus our Lord: in union with him
decisions.reason: Eternal life is found in Christ and given to those who belong to him, as in 5:21 and 8:1-2.
Balanced and Readable add "free" to bring out the contrast with wages.
Readable explains "in Christ Jesus", as in verse 11.
The word is a soldier's regular pay (m1). "Salario" and "sueldo" are the ordinary words for pay received for service.

decisions.choice: el don que Dios da gratis (B); como regalo (R)
decisions.reason: The gift is a gift of grace, not earned like wages (m2). Balanced says "da gratis" (gives free) for the English "free gift"; as in 3:24, "gratuito" is avoided because "gratuitamente" can also mean "for no reason". Readable says "regalo", as 3:24 does.
The word is a soldier's pay (m1). "Ujira" is pay earned for work or service; "mshahara" is a monthly salary and is also right. A reviewer may prefer "mshahara".

"Karama" is used in 1:11 and 12:6 for spiritual gifts given for service. Here the gift is eternal life itself, freely given by grace (m2), which "zawadi" (gift) says plainly; Balanced and Readable add "ya bure" (free), as the English says "free gift".

decisions.choice: "삯" (L); "품삯" (B, R) for the wages; "은사" (L); "거저 주시는 선물" (B, R) for the gift
decisions.reason: The wages are the regular pay a soldier earns (meaning decision); "삯", "품삯" are pay for work done. The gift is the word of 5:15-16, where Literal has "은사"; Balanced and Readable say "거저 주시는 선물" so the contrast with earned pay is plain.
